title: Hard–soft phase-ratio control of magnetic reversal and microwave absorption in Ni 0.5 Co 0.5 Fe 2 O 4 –SrFe 12 O 19  ferrite composites
content: Developing high-performance microwave absorbers that balance strong attenuation with broad bandwidth is critical for advanced electromagnetic wave management, yet tailoring interphase interactions to optimize specific performance metrics remains challenging. In this study, hard-soft Ni0.5Co0.5Fe2O4–SrFe12O19 ferrite nanocomposites with varying molar ratios (3 : 1 to 1 : 3) were synthesized via a citrate-assisted sol–gel route. Structural and magnetic analyses confirmed pure biphasic coexistence, demonstrating that an increased Ni0.5Co0.5Fe2O4 fraction promotes exchange-coupling-assisted cooperative magnetic reversal and elevates saturation magnetization. Crucially, positron annihilation spectroscopy uncovered the atomic-scale defect landscape governing dynamic loss. The intensity-weighted mean lifetime (τmean) evolved non-monotonically, peaking at 0.224 ns in the Ni0.5Co0.5Fe2O4/SrFe12O19 (2 : 1) composite (NCS-2) due to a maximum proliferation of interfacial open-volume defects and vacancy clusters (τ2 = 0.275–0.415 ns). Supported by strong high-momentum core-electron (3d/3p) annihilation features, this defect architecture maximizes interfacial polarization centers tightly coupled with active magnetic ferrite regions. Consequently, transmission-line calculations revealed a tunable performance trade-off governed by phase-ratio tuning: NCS-2 achieved an exceptional minimum reflection loss of −50.7 dB at 6.32 GHz (3.00 mm), whereas the 1 : 2 composite (NCS-4) delivered the broadest contiguous effective absorption bandwidth of 7.60 GHz at 2.00 mm. These findings establish that hard–soft phase-ratio engineering enables the independent tuning of absorption depth and operational bandwidth, offering a rational design strategy for ferrite-based microwave absorbers.
